articles.title: Courtois: "¿Vinicius? Sólo conozco a dos futbolistas que siempre están a su mejor nivel"
articles.standfirst: El portero belga analizó la victoria del Madrid ante el Leipzig en el Bernabéu
articles.summary: El portero belga analizó la victoria del Madrid ante el Leipzig en el Bernabéu
articles.body: Thibaut Courtois atendió a los medios de comunicación en la zona mixta del Santiago Bernabéu tras la victoria del Madrid (4-1) frente al RB Leipzig en la fase de liga de la Champions League. El guardameta belga, uno de los mejores del partido, analizó el estado de forma del equipo de cara al inminente Clásico liguero, defendió el rendimiento de su compañero Vinicius frente a las críticas y prefirió mantener un voto de confianza hacia la honestidad del colectivo arbitral y la herramienta del VAR. Victoria antes del Clásico: "Al final yo creo que hemos jugado buenos partidos, buenas victorias, una buena remontada en Roma y al final estamos con confianza para lo que viene y sabemos que va a ser un partido duro, pero si queremos recortar puntos en la Liga habrá que ir a ganar el partido". ¿Es favorito el Barça?: "Al final nunca se sabe hasta que juegas el partido ahí, yo creo que estamos bien, estamos con confianza y al final en la Liga han estado muy bien, pero yo confío en nuestro equipo que podamos ir a ganar. Es verdad que es en su casa, es un partido diferente cuando vas de visitante, pero yo confío en nuestro equipo y para mí los Clásicos, aunque a veces llega un equipo mejor que otro, para mí siempre son 50-50". Vinicius: "No, yo creo que está en busca de su mejor versión y estoy seguro que llegará con el apoyo del equipo, de la afición y creo que ha hecho un partido bueno, le he visto con acciones, con peligro y al final no siempre te salen las cosas. Un jugador que está cada temporada a su mejor nivel, ahora que yo solo conozco a dos, que son Cristiano y Messi, que los he visto casi cada año en su mejor nivel y aún así se les han criticado en varios momentos a dos de los más grandes de la historia. Al final es fútbol, yo creo que Vinicius es alguien que lleva nueve años jugando casi todo y por eso nosotros tenemos que ayudarle a buscar esa mejor versión, pero él es el primer entrenador que está contento, feliz y buscando su mejor versión. Dificultades fuera de casa: "En casa y fuera siempre son partidos diferentes y nos ha costado más hacer los partidos fuera, como en España, Roma, Elche y luego las dos derrotas de Betis, yo creo que a Betis merecimos más, ahí perdimos pero hicimos un buen partido. Es verdad que fuera de casa hay que mejorar, pero aún así creo que nos estamos haciendo bien ahora en la vuelta después del parón y estaremos con ganas del domingo y con lo que viene, porque ahora hay cuatro partidos fuera de casa y si no queremos desengancharnos de la liga, pues son tres partidos". ¿Tenéis miedo del arbitraje este fin semana?: "No, porque al final yo confío en los árbitros, confío que ellos van con la conciencia de hacer lo que ellos pueden hacer y que al final son humanos, pueden hacer errores, pero bueno, esperamos que no siempre son errores para un lado y no para otro. Y que cuando entre el VAR sean por cosas por las que de verdad vino el VAR. Desde 2018 que se introdujo era para cosas muy claras y yo siento que en la Liga entran demasiado. Y cosas que cuentan a principio de temporada, que nos comemos una hora de charla de los árbitros para que luego a la semana se estén equivocando y haciendo cosas al revés, pero yo como humano y como persona optimista, yo quiero creer que siempre van honestos al campo y como te digo, puedes equivocarte y por eso está el VAR, pero ya está".

articles.title: Saka injury 'does not look good' - how will Arsenal cope?
articles.summary: Mikel Arteta says the quadriceps injury Arsenal's Bukayo Saka picked up in the Champions League draw with Bayern Munich "does not look good at all".
articles.body:
Mikel Arteta says the quadriceps injury Arsenal's Bukayo Saka picked up in the 2-2 Champions League draw against Bayern Munich "does not look good at all".

The 25-year-old winger went down in the 10th minute at Allianz Arena - attempting to play a pass with nobody around him - and had to be replaced by Eberechi Eze, who went on to score the opening goal.

"They are a bit concerned. A player who has to come off with a really sharp pain is never good news but we have to wait and see," Arteta told TNT Sports.

Saka has had fitness issues in recent months and his game time was managed at the end of last season, as well as with England at the World Cup, because of an Achilles injury he picked up in March.

He missed the March international break and seven games for the Gunners, but returned to help them lift the Premier League title for the first time in 22 years.

Saka started the Champions League final defeat by Paris St-Germain but was substituted after 54 minutes, and only started three of England's eight games at the World Cup - scoring a hat-trick in the 6-4 third-place win over France.

The forward also had surgery on a hamstring injury he picked up in December 2024, which kept him out for 101 days in the 2024-25 season.

He made 49 appearances as Arsenal won the title last term, despite a stop-start season - as well as the Achilles issue, he pulled out of the warm-up against Leeds with a hip injury in January and a hamstring problem kept him out for about four weeks.

But he remains vital to the Gunners, whose win percentage is notably more impressive with him in the team.

Despite the loss of Saka early on in the game, Arsenal still produced a good performance and could have won the match late on after Declan Rice's late equaliser.

"The only negative is seeing one of their star players, Saka, having to pull up with an injury early in the first half," said Champions League Match of the Day pundit Nedum Onuoha.

"He was lying on the floor with his hand up and he knew he was in a bit of trouble, so now the concern will be how long he is out for.

"It's not necessarily something that means the team will struggle heavily, but there is a reason why he is regarded as one of the best players in this Arsenal team and is seen as being important for them."

After Saka's withdrawal Noni Madueke, who had started on the left wing, switched to the right and looked bright, while Eze scored the opening goal from the left after coming off the bench.

"This is one of the reasons their squad has been built the way it has been and I think Madueke and Eze did well on the wings today after Saka came off," added Onuoha.

"In terms of options, at this moment in time for Arsenal, it is not going to be an issue - they will miss the star power that he has, they still have plenty of other wide players who can step up and do the job while they wait for him to come back."

Arsenal's style of play has been criticised this season but, even before Saka's withdrawal, the Gunners played on the front foot and enjoyed more possession than their German opponents.

Losing Saka, who has scored four goals in 11 appearances in all competitions, will be tough to deal with.

But the Gunners have invested heavily in their squad over the past two summer transfer windows and have options.

Madueke can play on both wings, while summer signing Christos Tzolis - although currently out with a hamstring injury - has started the season well.

The Gunners also have 16-year-old Max Dowman as an attacking option, and the youngster has already shown that he can have an impact for the senior side after scoring in the Premier League last season.

Arteta, who was asked what the rest of the forward line will need to do in Saka's absence, said he was pleased with what he saw against Bayern.

"I think Ebs [Eze] had a great game. Not only the ball, but the actions. His overall performance, I think his commitment without the ball as well," he said.

"And when the other ones come in, I think they really contributed to this. First of all, the energy.

"And then to bring different tools that the team needed in that moment to get something out of the game. So, very pleased again."
authors: Alex Howell - Arsenal reporter in Munich

articles.title: How USC would have fared retroactively with a 24-team playoff
articles.summary: A 24-team playoff is reportedly coming to college football as soon as next season. Had it been introduced in 2014, which years would USC have made it?
articles.body:
Last week, it was revealed that a 24-team playoff is all but certainly coming to college football. Despite the proposal being extremely unpopular , the new system is reportedly set to take effect as soon as next year.

So how would this affect USC? Let's take a look back at the 12-year history of the College Football Playoff and see which years the Trojans would have made the field:

USC would have been the final team to make the playoff, squeaking in as the No. 24 seed. The Trojans would have visited No. 9 seed Ole Miss in a first round matchup.

Coming in at No. 25 in the final College Football Playoff rankings, USC would have been the first team out of the field.

USC would have been the No. 9 seed, just missing out on a first round bye. The Trojans would have hosted No. 24 seed Temple in a first round game at the Coliseum.

This time, USC would have gotten a bye, earning the No. 8 seed. The Trojans would have hosted a second round game against the winner of the first round matchup between No. 9 seed Penn State and No. 24 seed NC State.

After a horrific 5-7 season, USC would not have even come close to making the playoff.

The Trojans would have been the No. 22 seed and visited No. 11 seed Utah in a first round game. It would have been a rematch of a September meeting between the two teams at the Coliseum, which USC won 30-23.

The No. 17 seed Trojans would have visited No. 16 seed BYU in a first round game.

This was the worst USC football team of the modern era, with the Trojans finishing 4-8. They could have expanded the playoff to 48 and this team still would not have been worthy of a spot.

USC would have made it back to the playoff in 2022 as the No. 10 seed. The Trojans would have welcomed No. 23 seed NC State to the Coliseum for a first round matchup.

After starting the year 6-0, USC went 1-5 in its final six regular season games, leading to the Trojans missing the playoff.

A 6-6 regular season would have seen the Trojans not even sniff the bracket for the third time in four years.

USC would have returned to the playoff for the first time in three years as the No. 16 seed. The Trojans would have hosted No. 17 seed Arizona in a first round game at the Coliseum.

In 12 years, USC would have made the 24-team playoff seven times. The Trojans would have been a top eight seed once, between No. 9 and No. 16 three times, and been one of the final eight teams in three times.

articles.title: Bayern Munich’s Vincent Kompany delivers health update after Arsenal clash
articles.summary: The FC Bayern bossman battled illness heading into the big Champions League showdown this week.
articles.body:
Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany was waylaid this week by a viral infection with symptoms bothersome enough that it even affected his ability to move around on the sidelines in last weekend's match against RB Leipzig.

The Bavarians romped all over the Red Bull club, 6-1, but Kompany cut a subdued figure as he dealt with the effects of whatever virus he had contracted, which aggravated an old hip injury. It was bad enough that there were reports surfacing about Bayern's contingency plans—with assistant Aaron Danks taking charge as sideline gesticulator-in-chief should Kompany be a no-go for this week's hotly anticipated Champions League clash against Premier League champion Arsenal.

Thankfully, Kompany recovered in time to prowl the sidelines himself on Wednesday, and was even able to jump up and gesture at the officials following a questionable call or two. The contest, a high-quality affair with scintillating moments of brilliance from both sides, ended in a 2-2 draw .

"I'm doing better," Kompany shared at his post-match press conference (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ). "It's a normal human thing. As a coach, you want to do everything by yourself. I didn't listen to my body, and at some point my body told me: 'Stop now, man!' …that was it.

"Now I'm feeling better, otherwise I wouldn't be here."

PSA aside: it is respiratory virus season after all, and all sorts of nasties are floating around. It's not too late to go get your flu and other shots—for yourself and the community!

articles.title: Decoding the business of bringing Brazil, Uruguay, Panama to India for football friendlies
articles.summary: New Delhi: Bringing Brazil to India was not just about getting one of football's biggest names to play a match.
articles.body: New Delhi: Bringing Brazil to India was not just about getting one of football's biggest names to play a match. It was about negotiating with federations, securing the right venue, arranging travel and accommodation, ensuring security, maintaining the pitch and, ultimately, figuring out who will pay for it all.The financial stakes are substantial. An international friendly involving a World Cup nation can cost at least Rs 10 crore, while staging a match involving one of the biggest teams could push the bill to Rs 100 crore, according to Anuj Kichlu, director and CEO of Best of You, which helped facilitate India's friendlies against Panama, Brazil and Uruguay."It would happen depending on the team. But an international friendly of a World Cup nation kind of friendly will not come under 10 crores," Kichlu told TimesofIndia.com after the three friendlies in Bengaluru and Kolkata."I'm saying you take the cost of the team, the cost of their travel, the cost of the stadium, event, and that. So the lowest you'll get a World Cup team is at Rs 10 crores, and the highest it'll cost is even 100 crores for one match, depending on the team."The figures, he explained, cover considerably more than the fee for securing a team's appearance."It's appearance, logistics, flights, hotels, securities, player's safety, police, in-stadium branding, event management, insurances. Everything would be covered," he explained.The challenge, therefore, is not simply to bring a marquee team to India. It is to make the economics of the event work in a market where the appetite for international football is still developing.Who pays for the spectacle?There is no single business model for staging an international friendly. The financial structure depends on who initiates the event and what they hope to achieve.A private promoter may organise a match with the expectation of recovering the investment through ticket sales, sponsorships and broadcast rights. A football federation, meanwhile, may be driven by sporting objectives, including giving its national team exposure against stronger opposition.In the case of India's recent friendlies, the AIFF approached the Spain-headquartered Best of You to help bring international teams to the country. They acted as a match agent, negotiating with the visiting federations and coordinating arrangements for their participation. Commercialisation, including ticketing and broadcasting, was handled separately by the AIFF and its agencies.Kichlu was clear about the distinction."Yeah, they engaged agencies for sponsorship. They engaged agencies for ticketing. They had security agencies for private security. They engaged with several different vendors, 5-6 different vendors for different roles," said Kichlu, who leads the company's India office.They, meanwhile, are not necessarily the party carrying the event's commercial risk."It's two federations only, and we come in as match agents. So we are not actually a party on the contract, but we are match agents on the contract," he said on how the agreement is drawn.He explained that the agent's responsibilities included areas such as insurance and cancellation, rather than the commercialisation of the event.That separation is important. While the agent helps secure the teams and ensure contractual obligations are met, the federation and its commercial partners must work out whether the event can generate enough revenue to justify the expenditure.The problem with selling a Brazil matchBrazil was the centrepiece of the three friendly series, for which India opted against playing the FIFA ASEAN Cup, selected for its substantial fan following in India, especially in Kolkata. Panama was brought in as a preparatory opponent, while Uruguay was added later when an opportunity arose to secure the team at a comparatively favourable price during their tour of Japan and South Korea.But the appeal of a famous team does not automatically translate into a commercially successful event.Kichlu believes the market for international football in India has potential, although negative publicity surrounding the sport has affected confidence among both spectators and sponsors."I think there's a lot of negative news around (Indian) football. So as long as that's there, the appetite will be limited. But I think this one event will change the appetite for future events."He said the matches had generated interest in future fixtures, despite the commercial challenges."So already we are getting inquiries for future matches and stuff in India because this one was successful, other than commercially. If you see everything on the ground was quite successful."For sponsors, however, interest alone is insufficient. Brands want measurable evidence that an event can deliver an audience and provide value for their investment."Not only fans, even I'd say sponsors obviously are reluctant to associate with something if they don't have numbers and backing, right? So when you go to someone and say you're sponsoring a Brazil match and they ask you for data of another big match in India, you don't have a match to go by," he stated.The lack of comparable events makes it difficult to establish what sponsors should expect from a major international friendly. Television ratings, digital views and stadium attendance can offer useful indicators, but they need to be interpreted carefully.Kichlu pointed out that even television figures can be difficult to assess without knowing how long viewers watched. Digital views, too, do not necessarily reflect sustained engagement. The recent elation with viewership of the Indian Super League (ISL) is an example of keeping caution.The friendlies, meanwhile, could therefore serve as a reference point for future commercial decisions."So decisions in the future will be made based on these 3 matches and the UK tour (Unity Cup against Nigeria and Zimbabwe) and stuff like that," said Kichlu.For Indian football, the ability to turn those experiences into reliable audience data could be as important as securing the next marquee opponent.Why planning matters more than ticket pricesThe attendance at the Salt Lake Stadium for the friendlies against Brazil and Uruguay raised eyebrows. 51,402 came through the gates for the Brazil game and 37,307 for the contest against Uruguay. Different reasons have been suggested for the less-than-expected turnout. Kichlu believes the marketing window and the timing of the event played a significant role."I think the marketing for the match was pretty late, to be honest, because with the kind of prices they're charging for those tickets, it means it's not that people aren't willing to pay it," he said."I think it just needs more planning because people will dedicate budgets to this compared to something else, and I would say a lot of people would have committed money somewhere else," he continued.The short lead time also limited the opportunity to attract fans from outside Kolkata."And with a 2-3 week window only, people would have made other plans to travel to other places. Being a long weekend also, I would say a lot of the people from Bombay, Delhi, Bangalore, stuff like that, would have made other plans to go on holidays in other places."His argument is that a match involving Brazil should not be marketed only to the city hosting it. It has the potential to draw spectators from across India, but doing so requires advance planning."But if they had, say, a 2-and-a-half, 3-month notice, they would have probably planned towards this.""I think the disappointing thing was that the number of people from across India who traveled for the match was low compared to what you would expect for this kind of a match."Concerns about safety following the earlier Lionel Messi event in Kolkata had, he said, made some parents cautious about bringing their children to another high-profile football event."I think we have to work more on the family experience and obviously giving more time and with that, it'll work."He does not believe ticket prices and it coming two weeks before Durga Puja explain the lower attendance."To be honest, the pricing of the tickets, I've researched all over Asia and even countries who are as far as India, and people are willing to pay this and much more for these kind of matches.""So I don't think it's that much of the ticketing price. I think it's the people who are willing to pay for these tickets are the ones who didn't come to the stadium," he reasoned.Why government backing mattersIf ticketing and sponsorship alone cannot guarantee a return, who should pay for the difference?Kichlu believes government support can be crucial when a country is trying to establish itself as a destination for major international football."I think government should play more of a role, right? If they want to bring these events, like, any state government wants to bring these kind of events to their state, they'd have to also pitch in resources. That's exactly why Brazil went to Australia.""The two matches were funded by the Queensland state government. It was part of their objective to promote the state internationally."I think there's a lot of negative news around (Indian) football. So as long as that's there, the appetite will be limited. But I think this one event will change the appetite for future events.The investment, in such cases, is not necessarily intended to be recovered entirely through ticket sales. Governments may see international sporting events as a way to promote a destination, generate publicity and build the infrastructure and reputation required to host larger events.Kichlu said the economics in established football markets are different for such friendlies because ticketing and broadcast revenues are more predictable."In Europe, you can take a team and you can make it commercially viable because the market is there, people are willing to pay it."In emerging markets, he argued, the commercial foundations are not yet as secure."And if you don't do that, I don't think these events are economical to organise like it is in Europe, where you have a set ticket price you can charge. You know what broadcast rights you'll get. You know what sponsorship you'll get. Everything is starting at a base level. So you have to have backing," he finished.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: MLS Goalie Roman Burki Hospitalized After Scary Injury During St. Louis vs. Crew U.S. Open Cup Final
articles.summary: There was a scary scene in the second half of Wednesday's U.S. Open Cup final between the Columbus Crew and St. Louis City SC.
articles.body:
There was a scary scene in the second half of Wednesday's U.S. Open Cup final between the Columbus Crew and St. Louis City SC.

St. Louis goalkeeper Roman Bürki took an inadvertent knee to the head while making a save on a loose ball in front of his net. He remained down for a number of minutes before he was taken off the field on a stretcher as concerned fans chanted his name.

The broadcast said he was conscious and taken to the hospital.

Backup goalkeeper Ben Lundt entered the scoreless tie for St. Louis after play resumed.

Bürki entered Wednesday's contest with 28 starts during the 2026 MLS season for St. Louis. He has allowed 39 goals with 74 saves and four clean sheets.

This was also his fifth start in the 2026 U.S. Open Cup for his club, and he tallied two clean sheets in his previous four. He appeared on his way to another clean sheet before the injury and stood strong despite the Crew controlling the majority of play and creating chances in the first half.

St. Louis has a quick turnaround following Wednesday's game, so Lundt may be thrown into action beyond just the end of the U.S. Open Cup final.

It faces Real Salt Lake on Saturday when MLS play resumes.

articles.title: Mbappé: "Está bien que Vinícius esté triste"
articles.standfirst: "Vinicius tiene que estar orgulloso de quién es"
articles.summary: "Vinicius tiene que estar orgulloso de quién es"
articles.body: Kylian Mbappé, delantero del Real Madrid, afirmó que está "bien" que Vinícius esté triste porque eso significa que el jugador brasileño quiere mejorar para ayudar a su equipo y recuperar su mejor versión. Vinícius no firmó un gran partido y fue sustituido por Diomande en el minuto 70. Se marchó cabizbajo al banquillo y después de la victoria frente al Leipzig por 4-1, Mbappé animó a su compañero. "Es bien. Está bien que Vinícius esté triste porque él quiere dar mucho al equipo y a la gente. Tiene que estar tranquilo, orgulloso de quien es. Es un gran jugador que tiene una gran calidad", afirmó a Movistar Plus. También analizó su situación personal y reconoció que tiene que mejorar: "Estoy bien. Puedo hacer más. Soy parte de los jugadores que hay que exigir siempre más. Nunca es suficiente para un jugador como yo", explicó. Además, habló sobre la tercera victoria del Real Madrid: "Sabemos que cada punto es importante para entrar en los ocho. Tenemos que ganar un máximo de partidos, hemos ganado tres". Por último, habló sobre el clásico que disputará el Real Madrid el próximo domingo: "Hemos pensado únicamente en el partido de hoy. Lo que pasa el domingo, ahora lo podemos pensar. Antes el equipo no pensaba en el partido del domingo".

articles.title: Unai Emery maintains perfect Champions League start as Aston Villa sweep aside Viking 3-1 to extend Villa Park dominance
articles.summary: Aston Villa head coach Unai Emery guided his side to a third consecutive Champions League victory with a 3-1 triumph over Norwegian visitors Viking on Wednes...
articles.body:
Aston Villa head coach Unai Emery guided his side to a third consecutive Champions League victory with a 3-1 triumph over Norwegian visitors Viking on Wednesday. The hosts built a two-goal interval lead en route to securing two home wins alongside an opening away victory at Club Brugge, climbing to second in the standings.

Emery watched his team build upon their stellar 6-0 demolition of Fenerbahce by comfortably dispatching a stubborn Norwegian outfit that held Bayern Munich to a 3-3 draw last week. Ross Barkley and Emiliano Buendia scored before the break, and a Henrik Heggheim own goal sealed the victory, despite Peter Christiansen pulling back a late strike. The result marks a fifth win in six matches across all competitions for the hosts.

First-half blitz settles European contest

Villa dominated the opening exchanges as visiting goalkeeper Arild Ostbo denied Nicolas Jackson before Barkley broke the deadlock in the 23rd minute by glancing in Ibrahim Mbaye's precise corner kick. Buendia then doubled the advantage from the penalty spot 10 minutes later following a VAR review after Zlatko Tripic fouled Alysson inside the danger area.

The hosts effectively settled the contest in the 62nd minute when Heggheim inadvertently turned another dangerous Alysson delivery into his own net. Although Christiansen converted Kristoffer Askildsen's cross late on following a successful VAR check for offside, Villa comfortably secured another emphatic statement victory right there on home soil.

Historic milestones underline continental pedigree

Victory extended the Villans' extraordinary winning run in major European home fixtures to 12 consecutive matches , matching the longest historical streak achieved by any English club this century. The Midlands side also became the first Europa League holders since Manchester United in 2017-18 to triumph in their opening three matches of the tournament.

Furthermore, reaching 20 victories in just 30 European Cup and Champions League outings makes them the second-fastest team in history to hit that landmark , trailing only Real Madrid who required 29 matches. This incredible run highlights their status as serious contenders on the continental stage under the former Sevilla and Villarreal tactician.

Blockbuster Barcelona clash awaits Villans

Having firmly overcome their early sluggish start to the domestic campaign, Emery's resurgent squad sit proudly second in the elite European table after three rounds of fixtures. Their flawless continental campaign will face its ultimate test when they travel to face La Liga leaders Barcelona next month. Until then, the manager remains entirely focused on sustaining their impressive momentum across upcoming Premier League fixtures.

articles.title: Backup Ben Lundt makes key save in shootout as St. Louis beats Crew to win Lamar Hunt U.S. Open Cup
articles.summary: COLUMBUS, Ohio (AP) — Backup goalkeeper Ben Lundt made a key save in the penalty shootout of a 120-minute 0-0 tie with the Columbus Crew to help St. Louis Ci...
articles.body:
COLUMBUS, Ohio (AP) — Backup goalkeeper Ben Lundt made a key save in the penalty shootout of a 120-minute 0-0 tie with the Columbus Crew to help St. Louis City win the Lamar Hunt U.S. Open Cup on Wednesday night.

Timo Baumgartl gave St. Louis a 1-0 lead on the first penalty kick and then Lundt dove to his left to get a hand on Santiago Rodriguez's shot that deflected off the post.

St. Louis went 5 for 5 in the shootout, capped by Daniel Edelman's shot down the middle as goalkeeper Nicholas Hagen went the wrong way. Lukas MacNaughton, Chris Durkin and Damion Downs also scored.

St. Louis earned a spot in the 2027 CONCACF Champions Cup after securing the first major trophy in club history.

Columbus was seeking its second U.S. Open Cup title in club history.

Lundt entered the game in the 78th minute after starter Roman Bürki took a knee to the head while making a save. Bürki waved to the crowd while being carted off the field. Lundt came on in relief for his fourth appearance of the season.

It was the first U.S Open Cup final to go to penalties since 2015 when Sporting Kansas City beat the Philadelphia Union. The USOC is open to both professional and amateur clubs, but Major League Soccer teams have dominated the competition for more than two decades.

articles.title: Fabrizio Romano drops major Carrick update, claims situation has changed behind the scenes after “humiliating” defeat
articles.summary: Manchester United sank to a new low in Italy, suffering an embarrassing 4-1 defeat against Como, who are playing in the Champions League for the first time i...
articles.body:
Manchester United sank to a new low in Italy, suffering an embarrassing 4-1 defeat against Como, who are playing in the Champions League for the first time in their history.

Michael Carrick's reaction after the full-time whistle underlined his disappointment at his side's performance as he went to the away supporters and held up his hands in apology, without his players.

With United now winless in seven games across all competitions, Carrick's tactical ideas are clearly not working, and the gesture in Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia suggests the end of another managerial spell is on the horizon.

Fabrizio Romano details behind the scenes crisis at Manchester United

Fabrizio Romano addressed the situation on his YouTube channel, explaining why the feeling after the defeat against Como is different compared to other defeats under Michael Carrick .

Romano underlined the gravity of the situation after the absolutely "humiliating" loss by saying he is recording the video at 2 am in Italy to reveal the international tension at Manchester United.

"Tonight I'm recording this video, and this is at 2 am at night here in Italy. But the real difference between this game and the other games, the real change between this game and the other games, is also in the players," the Italian journalist stated.

"For the very first time we have players at Manchester United not so happy with the current situation. And that's something that we can consider as a big change compared to one, two, three, four, five weeks ago, when the season had almost started and Man United were already not at the best level possible."

After the defeat at Atletico Madrid, Lisandro Martinez appeared to back Carrick by criticising director of football Jason Wilcox.

However, this time, Romano insisted that "there is a feeling inside that not everyone is so happy with the current situation, and I'm also talking about the coach."

It is understood many players are not happy with the technical and tactical approach under Carrick at Carrington.

"That's why I think we have to be very careful with the Manchester United situation, because now we enter into a different territory," Romano added.

For now, United continue to publicly back Carrick, but as Romano highlighted, they did the same before sacking Erik ten Hag and then Ruben Amorim.

Given the Red Devils head coach is rapidly losing the support of his dressing room, we could hear an official statement from INEOS sooner rather than later.

articles.body:
With a crushing 4-0 victory over OL Lyonnes back in May, Barcelona sealed their fourth Women's Champions League success in six years.

On the domestic front they have won seven Spanish league titles in a row, and six of the past seven Copa de la Reina trophies.

The key to it all? Pere Romeu, their manager since 2024, points to continuity — and the special local quality behind it.

Romeu, 32, grew up with an architect for a father and a landscape designer for a mother. He chose a career in football, starting at smaller local clubs before first arriving at Barca as a youth coach in the men's section in 2017, where among the players he managed was Gavi.

He joined the women's senior team as part of then-manager Jonatan Giraldez's staff in 2021, following a short spell as an assistant coach to fellow Spaniard Ruben de la Barrera at Viitorul Constanta in Romania.

Now he has put his own mark on a side that won a European treble last season — before having to move on from the departure of Alexia Putellas to London City Lionesses this summer.

"Barcelona have done what others have not," says Romeu. "First, there has been a consolidated project and the club has anticipated things. It has put good resources into youth football, trusting the academy. And we have trusted young players to make the step up to the first team."

In terms of the coaching staff, too, Barcelona have shown trust — by consistently promoting from within and building on the work of previous leaders. Romeu's appointment continued a succession that began with Fran Sanchez in 2017. Lluis Cortes replaced Sanchez in 2019, Giraldez took over from Cortes in 2021, and Romeu followed Giraldez three years later.

When it comes to the investment Romeu highlights, the turning point came after a 4-1 defeat by OL Lyonnes in the 2019 Champions League final.

On the journey home, Cortes spoke with the team's captains about what needed to change. The club subsequently doubled training sessions and provided the resources needed to compete with Europe's best. Barca won their first Champions League in 2021 before Cortes handed over to Giraldez, who added two more.

Romeu continued the cycle in the 2026 final, a year after losing to Arsenal. He remembers the difference between the structure he joined in 2021 and the one that exists today.

"When I arrived there were two fitness coaches, now there are four," he says. "There were not two goalkeeping coaches, as there are now.

"What Barcelona have done very well is build a sporting project based on a lot of talented players from the club, good signings from outside and giving people who are prepared the confidence to manage, as our staff has been given. If we look at who leads each department, there is a very high level."

People who have worked with Romeu often highlight his deep knowledge of football and his appetite for discussing the game. His challenge is to make that knowledge accessible to his players.

"It is not about knowing a lot," he says. "It is about simplifying.

"You have to select very carefully what you want to communicate at a tactical and emotional level and convey it to your team.

"We try to specialise people within each area. Now we have a coach for set pieces, a coach for individual development and a coach for post-match analysis. That makes the volume of work high, but very specific, because everyone's responsibilities are divided up very clearly."

Romeu watches football throughout the week, sometimes turning to matches involving teams unrelated to Barcelona simply to switch off. But one team changed the course of his career: Pep Guardiola's Barca (2008-2012).

"What I saw amazed me, excited me. It gave me two feelings: the feeling of a football fan thinking, 'What a wonderful thing I'm watching', and the tactical feeling of a coach. What I saw was a real turning point in my life.

"Those years made me think a lot about how I wanted my team to develop when having such a high percentage of possession. That period helped me absorb a lot of the philosophy, culture and Barca DNA that people have always talked about."

That influence shaped Romeu's ideas about possession and attacking football. But his first Champions League final as Barcelona head coach, against Arsenal in 2025, left him questioning whether his team had stayed true to those principles.

"What hurt me most was that, at no point in the final were we the recognisable team we had always been," he says. "Not doing the collective things we had been doing was something I found difficult to digest."

A year later in Oslo, Barcelona reclaimed the trophy. For Romeu, the result was a reminder that the club's ambition cannot be separated from the way it plays.

"This year I want us to be even more dominant through our high pressing, because we have a slightly different profile of players. Every season, we have to adapt to the small differences in the squad we have.

"We have brought in a defender like Renee van Asten, who has the ability to step forward and press from behind, and that can allow us to do many things. That is where my excitement as a coach lies."

With Putellas leaving the club, Romeu saw Patri Guijarro as the natural leader to connect the experienced players with the younger generation.

"Once Alexia made the decision to leave, I was very clear that continuity had to come through Patri, because she was already a central figure between the veterans, the young players and the very young players," he says.

"I break football down into two things: the emotional and the tactical. Patri does both, perfectly. Every match. That a player who has won everything gives 100 per cent in training every single day is contagious to the whole squad."

Barca's next generation is already making its presence felt. Romeu describes the transition taking place within the squad as a positive one, with experienced figures alongside younger players who bring fresh energy. The performance of 18-year-old midfielder Clara Serrajordi in the Champions League final particularly impressed him.

"I knew she would start and that she would play a fantastic match," he says. "I was absolutely clear about it because her qualities fitted the kind of final I imagined. Mentally, you have to be a beast. You have to be prepared, and I never questioned whether she was ready."

For Romeu, La Masia remains Barcelona's defining advantage.

"It is our differentiating factor," he says. "There is an enormous amount of talent here. That is what always saves you in situations when you think, 'Perhaps this season we won't manage it', and suddenly a couple of young girls appear and surprise you.

"It is part of our identity, our DNA. Anything that takes us away from that takes us away from what we are as a club. I don't know a winning Barca, either men's or women's, that doesn't draw on a sense of belonging among players who come from La Masia or have been there."

However, Romeu still recognises that other models can work, including Michele Kang's multi-club approach (she owns Washington Spirit, OL Lyonnes and London City Lionesses).

He says those models "are very different, but equally legitimate".

"There is no one way that is better than another," he adds. "Both are valid.

"But here, given the type of club we are, we have to lean more towards the way we are doing things, and we will continue to be competitive in this way. The ambition is to fight for everything."

Editor's note: This interview took place a week before Barcelona requested an extension from FIFA in order to compete in the upcoming Women's Champions Cup because they do not comply with the world governing body's new regulations over female members of staff.

articles.title: Lillestrøm - Real Sociedad: El top 8 obliga a la Real a ganar hoy
articles.standfirst: El equipo txuriurdin debe sumar ante el Lillestrom su primer triunfo en esta Europa League si quiere seguir con opciones de lograr su objetivo inicial de clasificarse para los octavos
articles.summary: El equipo txuriurdin debe sumar ante el Lillestrom su primer triunfo en esta Europa League si quiere seguir con opciones de lograr su objetivo inicial de clasificarse para los octavos
articles.body: La Real Sociedad está obligada a ganar esta noche en su visita al Lillestrom noruego en su Arasen Stadion, si quiere seguir teniendo opciones de terminar en el top 8 de esta fase Liga de la Europa League y lograr de manera directa el pase a los octavos de final, porque de no hacerlo sólo las matemáticas harían factible ese objetivo, pero no las sensaciones y el calendario que restaría. Será un partido especial para el técnico local, Hans Erik Odegaard, que se enfrentará al equipo del que hace unos pocos años se hizo fan para ver triunfar a su hijo Martin. El ahora entrenador del Lillestrom vivió el inicio de la gran época que está viviendo la Real en los últimos años, con seis clasificaciones para Europa, la primera con su hijo Martin como una de las grandes estrellas, al ser su rendimiento espectacular, lo que llevó a que tuviera muchas ofertas y finalmente recalará en el Arsenal. Seguro que hoy seguirá el partido desde Londres y recordará ese gran año en San Sebastián. Odegaard padre recibirá hoy a un conjunto txuriurdin que, además de a su hijo, ha ido perdiendo a muchos futbolistas claves en sus éxitos más recientes, pero que les ha ido sustituyendo lo suficientemente bien como para jugar hoy contra él por haber ganado el título de Copa del pasado curso, vía idéntica por cierto por la que llegó el rival noruego. El regreso a la Europa League, eso sí, no ha empezado tan idílico como algunos vaticinaban, al sumar la Real sólo un punto en las primeras dos jornadas, lo que hace que los tres de hoy sean imprescindibles para el objetivo con el que arrancó la competición: estar en el top 8. De no llevárselos para San Sebastián, habría que empezar a pensar ya en estar en los 16 siguientes clasificados para la eliminatoria previa a los octavos de final. Matarazzo apunta a volver a realizar bastantes rotaciones, veremos si las seis o siete habituales o algunas menos por venir su equipo de un gran rendimiento en Málaga y el valor de los puntos. Con Marrero en la portería, Sergio Gómez regresará al lateral izquierdo, veremos si Zubeldia al derecho o Fort tiene continuidad. Turrientes podría tener una oportunidad en el doble pivote y en el ataque todo indica estarán Guedes y Sucic, veremos si también Zakharyan o se mantiene Óskarsson junto al indiscutible pero exprimido Oyarzabal. En cuanto al Lillestrom, llega a este partido igualado con la Real en el vigesimosegundo lugar de esta fase Liga, gracias al punto que sacó en la pasada jornada, cuando empató en el minuto 90 en su visita al Sparta de Praga. Antes, en la jornada inaugural, cayó de local por 1-2 ante el modesto Torreense de Portugal. Ambos tantos los hizo el veterano Thomas Olsen y en ambas citas en las rectas finales, que es en las que más suele encajar la escuadra de Matarazzo y en las que sale a jugar el ariete de 35 años. El defensa noruego Lars Ranger y el atacante angoleño Felix Vá son otros hombres destacados.

articles.title: El Málaga, entre los únicos tres equipos de Europa sin victorias en liga
articles.standfirst: Sólo el Le Havre francés y el Borussia Moenchengladbach alemán comparten tal condición en las cinco grandes ligas
articles.summary: Sólo el Le Havre francés y el Borussia Moenchengladbach alemán comparten tal condición en las cinco grandes ligas
articles.body: En esta semana de jornada continental donde todo el mundo mira a las competiciones de la UEFA, el Málaga se ha quedado como único representante español de una competición extraoficial en la que nadie quiere ganar. Literalmente, pareciese así. Los de Juanfran Funes no conocen la victoria en esta campaña 2026-27 y esa es la lucha que ahora tienen: no ser el último conjunto de las principales ligas europeas en conocer la victoria. De momento, tienen dos competidores dentro de lo que son las ligas domésticas de Francia, Alemania, Italia, Inglaterra y España, lo que siempre han sido denominadas como las cinco grandes competiciones domésticas del Viejo Continente. Con la victoria del Tottenham ante el Coventry del pasado lunes en la Premier League, los blanquiazules han quedado junto al Le Havre de la Ligue 1 y el Borussia Mönchengladbach de la Bundesliga. En contra de los malacitanos, hay que decir que en España la competición es la más avanzada en cuanto a calendario. Siete jornadas se han jugado en el país galo y seis en Alemania. El Le Havre es colista, igual que el Málaga, y solo ha sumado dos puntos, aunque, curiosidades de la vida, uno de ellos fue contra el actual líder de la liga francesa, el Olympique de Lyon. En Alemania, el Borussia Mönchengladbach está en una tesitura todavía peor que el equipo de la capital de la Costa del Sol. Los alemanes no han puntuado en seis jornadas y se han llevado goleadas prácticamente en todos sus partidos, lo que les ha provocado veinte goles en contra en este arranque de competición. El Málaga es el que más puntos tiene de los tres, también el que más partidos ha jugado, pero los andaluces han conseguido arrancar cuatro empates, evitando la derrota en casi la mitad de los encuentros que han disputado. En otras ligas menores también cunde el pánico en los colistas. En Portugal, el Estoril no ha ganado en ocho encuentros y es colista con dos puntos. En Holanda, el colista no ha ganado: el Willem II solo ha sumado dos puntos en nueve jornadas. En Bélgica es el Cercle Brugge el que todavía no conoce el triunfo, con tres empates en ocho encuentros. Por dejar un detalle final, también es malagueño el peor equipo de nuestro país en categoría federativa, es decir, de Primera a Tercera RFEF. Se trata del Málaga Juniors, que cierra el Grupo IX con cero puntos.

articles.title: Carles Martínez 'revive' al Leverkusen 'invencible' de Xabi Alonso: "En todas las competiciones aspiramos alto"
articles.standfirst: El conjunto de la 'aspirina' enlaza cinco victorias consecutivas y siete partidos sin conocer la derrota bajo el mando del técnico español
articles.summary: El conjunto de la 'aspirina' enlaza cinco victorias consecutivas y siete partidos sin conocer la derrota bajo el mando del técnico español
articles.body: La huella que dejó Xabi Alonso durante su estancia en el banquillo del BayArena será imborrable tras conducir al Bayer Leverkusen al título de la Bundesliga sin perder ningún partido... además de conquistar la POKAL y alcanzar la final de la Europa League. La temporada transición, iniciada por Ten Hag y finalizada con Kasper Hjulmand, derivó en la no clasificación a la Champions League. Con Carles Martínez Novell, sin embargo, parece que todo vuelve a estar en orden. "Nuestro objetivo sigue siendo competir de forma permanente al máximo nivel y seguir consolidando nuestra posición entre los clubes líderes de Europa. Estamos convencidos de que, con su convincente perfil como técnico, encaja muy bien con esta exigencia", explicaba Fernando Carro, CEO del Bayer Leverkusen, en la presentación del que fuese técnico del Toulouse. "Nos hemos ocupado intensamente de la cuestión de qué entrenador encaja mejor con la próxima fase de desarrollo del club", incidía Simon Rolfes, director deportivo. "Ha desarrollado con éxito a numerosos jugadores jóvenes en Toulouse y ha formado un grupo sólido con una plantilla de perfil internacional. A estas valiosas experiencias suma una gran competencia técnica adquirida durante su etapa en la academia de formación del Barcelona, que ahora trae consigo a Leverkusen". El proyecto volvía a transmitir ilusión tras la desbandada protagonizada por Wirtz, Frimpong, Xhaka o Tah el pasado verano. Y es que, más allá de Grimaldo, el Leverkusen no sufrió ninguna baja sensible... e invirtió cerca de 160 millones para fichar a Guéla Doué (30/Estrasburgo), Afonso Moreira (29.5/Lyon), Moussa Diaby (28/Al Ittihad), Miguel Gutiérrez (26/Nápoles), 'Facu' Medina (23/Marsella) y Kenneth Eichhorn (9/Hertha). "Xabi Alonso ha demostrado en el Bayer cómo se puede hacer. Lo que él ha conseguido es, por supuesto, fantástico. Voy a llamarle y estoy seguro de que hablará conmigo. Le conozco y sé que es un buen tipo y que solo quiere lo mejor para Leverkusen", confesaba un Carles Martínez Novell que, después de estrenarse con goleada al Wehen en la primera ronda de la POKAL, se vio sorprendido por el Elversberg en la primera jornada de la Bundesliga. "Tenemos que aprender y abrir los ojos". El equipo hizo autocrítica y, desde entonces, se están mostrando imparables... hasta el punto de haber 'revivido' al Bayer Leverkusen 'invencible' de Xabi Alonso: enlazan cinco victorias de forma consecutiva y siete partidos sin conocer la derrota. Como resultado, marchan a un punto del liderato que comparten Bayern y Dortmund en Bundesliga; segundos en la fase liga de la Europa League sin haber encajado ni un sólo gol; y en segunda ronda de la POKAL, donde se medirán al Nüremberg. "El objetivo es ganar cada partido y aspirar alto en todas las competiciones", reivindicaba un Carles Martínez Novell que, poco a poco, va impregnando su toque al Leverkusen... a la par que adaptándose a los recursos con los que cuenta en plantilla. Ha abandonado el 1-3-4-3 que solía utilizar en el Toulouse para dar paso a un 1-4-2-3-1... con matices: Quansah cierra como lateral bajo y permite que Miguel Gutiérrez haga de Grimaldo por izquierda. Arriba, Moreira, Diaby o Tella se encargan de dar amplitud, mientras que por dentro junta mucha gente de buen pie con Aleix García, 'Equi' Fernández o Ibrahim Maza. Los resultados, desde luego, le avalan. Además, también está 'sofisticando' su propuesta. Y es que, mientras que en el Toulouse priorizaba hacerse fuerte cerca de su área y asumir los menores riesgos en construcción, su Bayer Leverkusen es el equipo de la Bundesliga, sólo por detrás del Bayern, que más ocasiones claras crea (26); que más dispara (19.7) por partido; y que más goles marca (16). Todo ello, siendo el segundo en términos de posesión (57.7%), pases por secuencia de ataque (4.44) y altura de la línea defensiva (66.6 m). "Empiezo a reconocer cómo me imagino a mi equipo. Pero todavía estamos lejos del nivel que realmente podemos alcanzar. Sé que la plantilla es muy buena", dijo Carles Martínez Novell antes de la remontada contra el Friburgo, que marchaba líder de la Bundesliga hasta entonces, el pasado fin de semana. "Para mí, no solo son importantes los resultados, sino también la imagen que ofrece el equipo". En la visita al OFI Creta tratará seguir transitando por esta línea. De su mano, el Leverkusen vuelve a ser 'invencible'.

articles.title: 'Mac Anfield', la pesadilla de LaLiga
articles.standfirst: El '10' del Liverpool ha anotado cinco de sus ocho goles en Champions a equipos españoles
articles.summary: El '10' del Liverpool ha anotado cinco de sus ocho goles en Champions a equipos españoles
articles.body: El 'MVP' fue para Rio Ngumoha, pero perfectamente podría haber ido a parar a manos de Alexis Mac Allister (Santa Rosa, 1998). El '10' del Liverpool inició la remontada ante el Villarreal (4-3) en Champions... y la remató. El internacional argentino anotó el momentáneo 1-2 en el 36' al cabecear un córner botado por Kostas Tsimikas y marcó el 3-2 en el 65': apareció desde atrás para rematar un 'pase de la muerte' de Ngumoha. "No soy alto, pero me encanta llegar al área. Saben que me gusta atacar el primer palo. Me gusta mucho. También marqué un gol así en el Mundial. Fue un buen cabezazo. Es cierto que no es algo que practique mucho. Mi padre es un poco más bajo que yo, pero también era bastante bueno en el juego aéreo, así que quizás sea algo que heredé de él. En el segundo gol, Rio estuvo increíble", confesaba a 'Amazon Prime'. El ex del Brighton, fichado en 2023 a cambio de 42 millones de euros, se ha convertido en la 'pesadilla' de LaLiga: el 62,5% de los goles que ha marcado en Champions (cinco de ocho) los ha marcado contra equipos españoles. Cabe recordar que, este curso, ya le marcó al Atlético (2-1) en el debut. Según 'Mister Chip', sólo Josip Ilicic (71,4%, cinco de siete) y Alexandre Pato (66,6%, cuatro de seis) presentan un porcentaje mayor. LaLiga lo sufre mientras otro español, Andoni Iraola, lo disfruta. Es recíproco. "Desde el primer día empecé a ver algo especial. Es un buen tipo, y el cuerpo técnico también. Vamos por buen camino, pero tenemos que trabajar duro y darlo todo. Ojalá podamos ganar algunos trofeos", asegura el argentino. Analizando los goles de Mac Allister en Champions se da otra casuística, si cabe, más singular: todos sus tantos los ha marcado en Anfield. Es la primera vez, según 'Opta', que un jugador con, al menos ocho goles en la Liga de Campeones, marca todas sus dianas en el mismo estadio. Un estadio al que espera seguir ligado -tiene contrato hasta 2028- muchos más años. "Me entristece ver que no conseguí un nuevo contrato, pero todavía hay tiempo. Hubo opciones para salir este verano. Daré el 100 % hasta el último día que esté aquí", aseguró recientemente. Tras el partido contra el Villarreal, sin embargo, quiso decir 'digo donde había dicho Diego': "Cuando dije lo que dije, se trataba más bien de mis sentimientos. Es su decisión y está bien. Hago lo mejor que puedo y al final veremos qué pasa", subraya 'Mac Anfield', la 'pesadilla' de LaLiga.

articles.title: El 'King' de Arbeloa: "Es el jugador más elegante de todos los clubes con los que he estado vinculado"
articles.standfirst: Josh King (19 años) es, según 'Gradient Sport', el 'Jugador Más Mejorado' de la Premier
articles.summary: Josh King (19 años) es, según 'Gradient Sport', el 'Jugador Más Mejorado' de la Premier
articles.body: "Mis jugadores creen en nuestras ideas. Juegan de la manera en que queremos jugar, incluso cuando perdemos", asegura, orgulloso, Álvaro Arbeloa. Una filosofía que representa mejor que nadie Joshua David Steven King (Kingston upon Thames, 2007). "¡Qué jugador! Es increíble. Ya conocía su talento, pero con calidad no basta para este tipo de jugadores. Necesitan hacer números y marcar goles", vaticinaba el exentrenador del Fulham en pretemporada. El inglés, internacional sub 21, tomó nota: acumula dos goles en 10 partidos este curso. En la victoria ante el recién ascendido Hull City (1-0), con Arbeloa cuestionado, se echó el equipo a la espalda: fue el jugador que más ocasiones de gol generó (3) y que más tiros a puerta registró (2). De hecho, fue escogido 'MVP'. "Creo que fuimos realmente valientes. Jugamos como un equipo que sabía lo que tenía que hacer y trabajamos duro los unos por los otros. Estos tres puntos eran importantísimos", reconocía Josh King, que, según el 'Power Ránking' de 'Gradient Sport', es el 'Jugador Más Mejorado' (+21,7, de 62 a 84,8) de la Premier con respecto a la temporada pasada. "Su índice total (84,8) le sitúa como el segundo centrocampista ofensivo mejor valorado y con la octava puntuación más alta de la Premier", sugiere 'Gradient Sport'. Es, también, el cuarto con mayor volumen de conducciones de balón (77,6) y el sexto que más tiros a puerta registra (9) en la Liga inglesa. "Es un jugador de gran talento. No tiene límites. Tiene el talento, la mentalidad y el carácter: lo tiene todo para convertirse en un jugador de primerísimo nivel", insistía Arbeloa antes del comienzo de la Premier. Una tesis respaldada por Huw Jennings, director de desarrollo futbolístico del Fulham: "Disfruto viéndole. Es el jugador más elegante y ágil de todos los clubes con los que he estado vinculado". "Tiene todas las cualidades que necesitas como jugador de ataque: velocidad, conducción, visitón de juego, olfato de gol... Me gusta mucho y creo que va a tener un buen futuro. Espero que no se le suba el ego", apunta Ray Houghton, exjugador del Fulham. "Es un talento fantástico. Tiene 19 años y no le da miedo recibir el balón. Quiere la pelota, quiere crear ocasiones, quiere marcar goles", remarca Bobby Zamora, finalista de la Europa League con los 'cottagers' en 2010. "King es 'top'. Es increíble, pero debe seguir desarrollándose y trabajar su finalización. Puede añadir goles a su juego. Parece un buen tipo que quiere aprender", señala Tim Sherwood, ex de Tottenham y Blackburn, en 'Sky Sports'. En el Fulham de Arbeloa empieza a asomar un nuevo 'King'.

articles.title: Mikel Arteta admits Bukayo Saka injury 'doesn’t look good at all' after winger limps off during Arsenal's 2-2 draw with Bayern Munich
articles.summary: Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has expressed serious concern over Bukayo Saka's fitness after the England winger suffered an early injury during Wednesday's Ch...
articles.body:
Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has expressed serious concern over Bukayo Saka's fitness after the England winger suffered an early injury during Wednesday's Champions League clash in Germany. The attacker limped off inside the opening exchanges before the Premier League champions fought back to earn a battling point against Bayern Munich.

Arteta fears Saka faces a spell on the sidelines after his talismanic wide man sustained a suspected thigh injury against the German champions. The Gunners forward pulled up unchallenged while attempting a routine pass in the 10th minute and had to be withdrawn immediately. Wednesday's hard-earned point at the Allianz Arena was consequently overshadowed by the prospect of losing a key player amid a gruelling calendar.

Substitute impact precedes German turnaround

Introduced in Saka's place, Eberechi Eze broke the deadlock in the 25th minute from an incisive Martin Odegaard pass after VAR overturned an initial offside flag. However, the visitors led for just 10 minutes before England captain Harry Kane split the backline from midfield to tee up Alphonso Davies and subsequently sent goalkeeper David Raya the wrong way from 12 yards after his shot struck Jurrien Timber's hand inside the box.

Sharing the medical staff's initial concerns over the winger's withdrawal when speaking to TNT Sports , Arteta said: "They [the medical team] are a bit concerned. A player who has to come off with a really sharp pain is never good news, but we have to wait and see."

Relentless intensity takes physical toll

Arsenal eventually salvaged a draw in the 82nd minute when Declan Rice exchanged passes with substitute Viktor Gyokeres and drilled into the bottom corner before Manuel Neuer produced an acrobatic stop to deny Timber a late winner. Remarkably, it marked only the second time in European Cup or Champions League history that the Gunners have scored first, fallen behind and avoided defeat, repeating their 2-2 stalemate against Bayern in April 2024.

Asked during his post-match press conference whether the relentless fixture schedule contributed to the injury, Arteta added: "Against Lille, he didn't start the game. Then he started the game at the weekend. And then it's very early in this game.

"The level of intensity these games require is something incredible. You could see what happened in the PSG-Barcelona game [on Tuesday]. This is man-to-man for 96 minutes. Every action. There's no breathing.

"The strength, the quality, the attention, the level that you need is unbelievable because it's the highest level. Those things happen, unfortunately. It doesn't look good at all, but we have to wait and see."

Medical scans determine recovery timeline

Saka will now undergo further scans back in north London to establish the exact severity of his thigh problem and how long he will be unavailable. Losing such an influential figure would be a major blow for Arteta as he prepares his squad for their upcoming domestic Premier League commitments this weekend . Consequently, Eze and Gyokeres will be relied upon to step up in attack.

articles.body:
Allianz Stadium sets the stage for a handsomely-looking UEFA Europa League clash between Juventus and Rennes. It's a chance for both sides to put last weekend's disappointments behind them and turn the page.

Lazio shocked Turin on Sunday, strolling to a dominant 3-0 win and heightening the pressure on head coach Luciano Spalletti. It's been an underwhelming start to the season for Juventus, who have won just three of their last seven outings in all competitions (W3, D2, L2), though two of those three wins came in the Europa League.

After a thumping 5-0 victory over NEC Nijmegen on the opening matchday, Juventus fought back from an early deficit to beat Celta Vigo 2-1 on the road last week. As a result, they head into round three as one of just ten teams with a 100% record in this season's league-phase campaign. However, Rennes could be a tricky opponent.

Like Juventus, Franck Haise's side suffered defeat in their domestic championship at the weekend. Paris FC eked out a pulsating 4-3 win over Rennes in the last Ligue 1 round, knocking Les Rouge et Noirs off a two-game winning streak in all competitions. A come-from-behind 2-1 home triumph over OFI Crete in the last Europa League round was part of that run, which was a perfect response to a dull 0-0 draw at Sturm Graz on day one.

Spalletti can only hope that a return to the Europa League could be a welcome distraction from Juventus' domestic slump. The record-time Italian champions already trail Serie A pacesetters Inter by eight points and are seemingly out of the Scudetto race after just seven league rounds.

However, Juventus could salvage what promises to be another heartbreaking Serie A season with a long-awaited European success. Their last Europa League triumph came in the early 1990s, and lifting the trophy this term would provide a much-needed morale boost and restore some pride amid immense domestic struggles.

Juventus can draw confidence from winning their last four home outings in major European competitions, their longest such run since December 2021. Furthermore, the Bianconeri have won both previous meetings with Rennes, securing a 4-2 aggregate victory in the 1999 UEFA Intertoto Cup final.

Visiting Italian clubs spells disaster for Rennes, who have lost all four previous away clashes against Serie A opposition. Yet, the visitors' promising Europa League start, highlighted by remarkable defensive discipline, suggests they could buck that trend on Thursday despite long odds.

Haise's men lead the competition this season for the lowest expected goals against (0.79) and fewest shots faced (13). Another solid defensive performance may be vital as Rennes bid to overcome notorious inconsistency (W2, D1, L2) and put a woeful three-game winless away streak to an end (D1, L2).

It's worth noting that Les Rouge et Noirs failed to get on the scoresheet in two of those three winless outings. Moreover, despite their impressive defensive exploits at the start of this season's league phase, the French side conceded at least three goals in four of their last six away games in all competitions (W1, D1, L4).

Diminutive winger Francisco Conceicao dislocated his shoulder against Lazio, joining long-term absentees Kenan Yildiz, Khephren Thuram, Jeff Ekhator, Kamil Grabara, and captain Manuel Locatelli on the sidelines. With the Portuguese star ruled out, Kerim Alajbegovic could make another start for Juventus, with Nick Woltemade expected to lead the line ahead of Randal Kolo Muani.

Meanwhile, French forward Esteban Lepaul remains Rennes' only missing player ahead of this trip. Lepaul's absence could make room for Lazio loanee Boulaye Dia to partner up with Ludovic Blas and Issa Soumare in attack.

Juventus vs Rennes Potential Starting Lineups

Juventus (3-4-2-1): Vicario; Kalulu, Gatti, Kelly; Celik, Luiz, Sarr, Cambiaso; McKennie, Alajbegovic; Woltemade.

Rennes (4-3-3): Samba; Reynolds, Cresswell, Ait Boudlal, Nagida; Szymanski, Rongier, Camara; Blas, Dia, Soumare.

Spalletti is running out of excuses and can't afford another slip-up if he's to solidify his position in the dugout. Despite lacking several first-team stars, Juventus head into proceedings as favorites to continue their flawless Europa League start and return to winning ways against travel-sick Rennes.

Both sides have demonstrated their capacity to score in abundance so far, suggesting a high-scoring contest could be on the cards as well.

articles.title: Mijatovic le muestra el camino al cabizbajo Vinicius en el Madrid tras el impacto de Diomande
articles.standfirst: "Me falta un poquito más de Vinicius y estoy convencido de que lo va a recuperar. Hay que dejarle un poquito de tiempo y no hay que presionarle demasiado"
articles.summary: "Me falta un poquito más de Vinicius y estoy convencido de que lo va a recuperar. Hay que dejarle un poquito de tiempo y no hay que presionarle demasiado"
articles.body: Pedja Mijatovic, jugador del Real Madrid de 1996 a 1999 y director de fútbol de equipo blanco de 2006 a 2009, analizó en el programa 'El Larguero' la situación que vive Vinicius en el Real Madrid tras el impacto del joven Yan Diomande en el equipo del "viejo lobo Mourinho". La tristeza con la que abandonó un cabizbajo Vinicius el campo al ser sustituido por Diomande en el minuto 70 del partido de Champions que el Madrid ganó 4-1 al RB Leipzig no pasó inadvertida para el de Podgorica. "Me falta un poquito más de Vinicius y estoy convencido de que lo va a recuperar. Hay que dejarle un poquito de tiempo y no hay que presionarle demasiado", le empezó argumentando el exfutbolista de 57 años a Manu Carreño. Mijatovic subrayó que "con Diomande podemos tener un jugador que puede marcar la diferencia y eso no quiere decir que sea mejor que Vinicius, pero en este caso puede tranquilamente recuperar su mejor forma de jugar. Creo que no debería tener ninguna prisa. Hay que esperarle y seguramente llegarán sus mejores tiempos". La postura de Mijatovic sobre Vinicius coincide con la de Kylian Mbappé, que tras el partido contra el RB Leipzig dijo sobre el brasileño que "está bien que Vinícius esté triste porque él quiere dar mucho al equipo y a la gente. Tiene que estar tranquilo, orgulloso de quien es. Es un gran jugador que tiene una gran calidad". Pedja Mijatovic puso sobre la mesa los nombres de los dos futbolistas del Real Madrid a los que vio más en forma ante el RB Leipzig, Jude Bellingham y Thibaut Courtois. "Bellingham está haciendo un grandísimo trabajo, jugando francamente bien y es un jugador fundamental en el equipo. Transmite mucha confianza y Mourinho cuenta mucho con él porque los jugadores le admiran. Da siempre el cien por cien", compartió. Sobre Courtois sentenció que es "el mejor portero del mundo". "No solo este año, sino también años atrás. Courtois cransmite muchísima confianza y sus paradas son tan importantes como los goles o las jugadas que crean sus compañeros. La seguridad que transmite es fundamental para un equipo grande", apuntó.

articles.title: La luz en la noche
articles.standfirst: Las cuatro esquinas: victoria, calma, Celta, fútbol
articles.summary: Las cuatro esquinas: victoria, calma, Celta, fútbol
articles.body: Ay, ese Madrid de Güler que nos da la paz, que encuentra el sentido sedante o fulgurante del centro del campo; ese Madrid de Valverde que inunda con su fuerza el lugar que ocupe del campo, jamás despistado, jamás perdido entre la cal de la yerba. Ese Madrid de Güler que lleva un puñal brillando cerca del pecho del enemigo, pases llenos de aire libre, pases que alejan el miedo de una derrota. Ese Madrid de Valverde que nunca se para, que jamás se hunde en el desierto de la ausencia, que agita, que destierra el miedo. Ese Madrid de Güler que levanta el ánimo de un público ávido de fuerza y belleza y hambre de ser, vencer, oscurecer las luces del enemigo. Ese Madrid de Mbappé que impone una velocidad hambrienta, ganas de superar cualquier herida, como Vinicius, que llegará si los pitidos de él se olvidan; ese Madrid de Cucurella, que ofrece la garra perdida, el sentido de jamás desesperar porque los sueños no existen si no existe la esperanza; el de Bellingham, que volverá a su estela goleadora y asesina. Diomande, la pantera. La versatilidad de Camavinga, que ya no está quemado por el fallo del Múnich. El toque de Bernardo Silva aclarando el panorama. La fiereza infranqueable de Rüdiger… que llegue ya el Clásico a ver esa goleada del Barça. Grande Courtois, siempre. Este es otro Madrid. Mi amigo Manuel Villanueva, que hizo una vida dirigiendo los contenidos de Mediaset, me confesó que para él, el Celta es un sentimiento, una emoción, una forma de ser y de vivir; y el celtismo es esa comunión entre afición y equipo en la que siempre hay de todo: miedo, amor, esperanzas, deseos y pasión; y una generosidad inmensa de aportar lo propio a lo común. En Galicia ha llovido mucho durante mucho tiempo, pero su corazón no se ha desteñido de su inmarcesible azul celeste. Ahora se integra como miembro del Consejo de Administración de su equipo del alma. Gana el Celta y gana Manolo, que siente vibrar su sueño en la realidad. En la noche de París, que huele a gomas quemadas y suenan por las esquinas los gritos de la revuelta, vimos un gran partido de fútbol. Mi amigo culé casi lloró de lo bien que jugó el Barça. Y lloró del todo cuando miró la faltriquera y había cuatro goles clavados a fuego. La emoción subió del césped hasta el lugar más recóndito del mundo, por ejemplo el bar Juani, donde me puse a gritar y llorar con los culés, que ya saborean la victoria del Clásico. El fútbol lo inventó un niño que juega a los dados, y dar por vencido a un contrario puede tener castigo. Qué gran partido vimos. Fútbol de noche y goles. Belleza entre el humo de los que protestan por tener una esperanza y un futuro.
